title: Taiwanese American Student Association @ Ohio State University
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Student Association (TASA) at The Ohio State University is a registered student organization focused on exploring Taiwanese American identity and culture on the Columbus campus. Its founding year is not stated on available first-party sources, though the organization’s official website is hosted on OSU’s org.osu.edu platform and its 2026–2027 constitution is on file with OSU Student Activities. TASA is open to all students regardless of identity or background.

According to TASA’s official university website, the organization exists “for those interested in examining the many facets of the Taiwanese American identity.” Its constitution further describes the organization’s purpose as fostering “a welcoming community that promotes awareness, understanding, and appreciation of Taiwanese and Taiwanese American culture, history, and identity,” and supporting opportunities for cultural education, leadership development, and cross-cultural dialogue. Past documented events include Taiwanese breakfast gatherings, bubble tea nights, and the annual Moon Fest cultural showcase, which has featured performances from multiple student organizations.

TASA maintains an active Instagram presence at @tasaosu (984 followers, 224 posts as of 2026) and a Facebook page at facebook.com/tasaosu. The organization also communicates via Discord and email. An older WordPress site (osutasa.wordpress.com) and a Weebly site (tasaohiostate.weebly.com, © 2012) exist but appear dormant; the current primary web presence is the OSU-hosted site.
